# DocFlow library — code audit

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Commit:** `50b0deb` (`fix(citations): give imported CSL styles a stable identity and a way out (#360, #361)`)
**Scope:** `packages/core`, `packages/layout-engine`, `packages/plugins`, `packages/vue`, `packages/element`, `packages/export`
**Reviewer:** AI agent (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), `ponytail-audit`
**Status:** snapshot. Track the work in GitHub issues; do not edit this file after merge.

---

## What this repo does

This is the **library half of DocFlow**: an embeddable, paginated, A4-style document
editor built on TipTap/ProseMirror and Yjs. The deployable application (web UI + API
server + database) is not here; it lives in `Kedata-Indonesia/docflow-app`.

**Load assumed:** one editor per browser tab, documents of roughly 1–100 pages, 2–10
people collaborating in a room, typing continuously. There is no server code in this repo,
so "load" means main-thread work per keystroke and per layout pass, plus the browser
resources a mounted editor holds.

**Method:** read the entry points and the main data paths (editor creation, paste, layout,
collaboration, export, AI, citations, headers/footers), traced what each one writes and
where; ran the unit suites; reproduced the encoding finding with a byte-level check; added
a documentation link gate while reorganising `docs/`.

All unit suites pass: **89 test files** across the six packages (`vue`: 40 files / 204
tests; `element`: 6 tests; the rest pass as well). Lint, typecheck, and the Playwright e2e
suite were **not** run for this audit.

## Must fix

### 1. RTF export turns every non-ASCII character into garbage

`packages/export/src/rtf.ts:3-16`

**What this is.** RTF export runs the document through `plainTextFromHtml()` and writes the
result into a file whose header declares `\ansi\ansicpg1252` (Windows Latin-1). The string
is then put into a `Blob`, which encodes it as UTF-8 (`packages/export/src/index.ts:80-81`).

**Problem.** RTF is a byte format. Any character above `0x7F` must be written as an RTF
escape (`\uNNNN?`), not as UTF-8 bytes. Read back as Latin-1, `—` becomes `â€”`,
`“kutipan”` becomes `â€œkutipanâ€`, `café` becomes `cafÃ©`, and an emoji becomes four junk
characters. Indonesian documents routinely contain curly quotes and en/em dashes, so the
export is visibly broken. The `title` is interpolated raw (line 12): a title containing
`{` or `\` corrupts the RTF group structure, and Word may refuse to open the file.

**Reproduction.** The byte sequence for `—` in the generated string is `e2 80 94` (UTF-8);
`new TextDecoder('windows-1252').decode(...)` renders `â€”`.

**Fix.** Add one escaper used by both the body and the title: `\` → `\\`, `{` → `\{`,
`}` → `\}`, newline → `\par\n`, any code unit above `0x7F` → `\u<code unit>?` (and a
`?` fallback already covers the ANSI reader). Keep `\ansicpg1252`.

**If we skip it.** Every downloaded RTF from a real document is corrupted, and titles with
braces produce an unopenable file.

**Issue title:** `fix(export): escape non-ASCII and title in RTF output`

---

### 2. `<docs-editor>` throws if it is ever re-attached to the page

`packages/element/src/DocsEditorElement.ts:45-48` (and `62-65`)

**What this is.** `connectedCallback()` unconditionally calls
`this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' })`. `disconnectedCallback()` only removes the inner Vue
element and clears `_shadowRoot`; the browser keeps the shadow root attached to the host.

**Problem.** `el.remove(); document.body.append(el)` calls `attachShadow` a second time on
the same host, which throws `NotSupportedError` ("Shadow root cannot be created on a host
which already hosts a shadow root"). This is a normal sequence for hosts that move the
element (modals, drag-and-drop, framework re-parenting) — the element ends up blank with an
uncaught exception, and the surviving shadow root is never reused.

**Reproduction.**

```js
const el = document.createElement('docs-editor')
document.body.append(el)   // works
el.remove()
document.body.append(el)   // throws NotSupportedError
```

There is no mount test for the element: `packages/element/src/__tests__/element.test.ts`
only exercises `_buildProps()` and registration.

**Fix.** Create the shadow root once and reuse it:

```ts
this._shadowRoot ??= this.shadowRoot ?? this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' })
this._shadowRoot.replaceChildren()
```

Then rebuild the `<style>` and Vue element inside it. Add one connect → disconnect →
reconnect test.

**If we skip it.** Any host that moves or remounts the element gets a blank editor and an
uncaught exception, with no diagnostic.

**Issue title:** `fix(element): make <docs-editor> survive disconnect/reconnect`

---

### 3. Host `modelValue` writes are ignored after mount

`packages/vue/src/components/DocsEditor.vue:104` → `packages/vue/src/composables/useEditor.ts:31-45`

**What this is.** `modelValue` is read once when the component sets up
(`modelValue: props.modelValue`) and passed to `createEditor` as initial content. Nothing
watches `props.modelValue`; `useEditor` watches `editable` and the collaboration
room/provider, not content. `README.md` documents the prop as "Two-way bound via
`v-model`".

**Problem.** After the first render, the host has no way to replace the document through
the public API. Concrete paths that break:

- **Version history.** The library's own `HistorySidebar` emits `restore-snapshot` /
  `preview-snapshot` for the host to apply; the only way for the host to apply them is to
  write `modelValue`. That write is a no-op, so preview/restore silently does nothing.
- **Document switching.** A host that changes `modelValue` when the route/document id
  changes keeps showing the old document unless it remounts the component with a `:key`
  (undocumented).
- **Web component.** `<docs-editor content="...">` is listed in `observedAttributes`, so
  `attributeChangedCallback` re-applies props — but the Vue component ignores the new
  `modelValue`, so changing `content` does nothing.

**Fix.** Watch `() => props.modelValue` and apply the value with
`editor.commands.setContent(value, { emitUpdate: false })`, guarded by a `lastEmitted`
reference so the editor's own `update:modelValue` does not loop back. Skip the watcher in
collaboration mode: the Yjs document is authoritative there, and local seeding is
deliberately disabled.

**If we skip it.** The documented `v-model` contract is false; snapshot restore and
document switching cannot work through the library API.

**Issue title:** `fix(vue): apply host modelValue changes after mount (or document the remount requirement)`

## Should fix

### 4. DOCX export silently deletes blank paragraphs

`packages/export/src/docx/nodes.ts:172-175`, `packages/export/src/docx/index.ts:109-121`

**What this is.** A paragraph with no text runs is dropped: `mapBlockNode` returns `[]`
when `children.length === 0`, and the top-level walk only pushes a `Paragraph` when
`runs.length > 0`.

**Problem.** Blank lines are content in word processors: users press Enter twice to
separate sections, and the exported DOCX reflows without the gap. Related edge on the same
code path: the shared inline mapper skips `image` nodes, so an image-only paragraph inside
a list item or heading loses the image (top-level paragraphs split images out separately;
headings and list items do not).

**Fix.** Emit `new Paragraph('')` for an empty paragraph, and let the list/heading paths
pass image nodes to `imageToDocxParagraph()` instead of dropping them. Add one export test
with `[paragraph "A", paragraph (empty), paragraph "B"]`.

**If we skip it.** Exported contracts and reports do not match the layout the user
approved on screen.

**Issue title:** `fix(export): keep empty paragraphs and images in DOCX`

---

### 5. `collaborationExtensions(options)` opens a connection nobody can close

`packages/core/src/Collaboration.ts:326-329`

**What this is.** The function accepts either a `CollaborationSetup` or plain
`CollaborationOptions`. In the options case it calls `createCollaboration(options)`
internally and keeps only the extensions:

```ts
const setup = 'ydoc' in options ? options : createCollaboration(options)
```

**Problem.** That setup owns a Y.Doc, an awareness instance, and (for `provider:
'websocket'` or `'webrtc'`) a live network provider. The caller receives only
`AnyExtension[]`, so there is no `destroy()` handle: the socket stays open after the editor
unmounts. The `whenReady` sync gate (#117) is also bypassed for that path.

**Fix.** Delete the options branch and require a setup — every internal caller already
passes one — or return `{ extensions, setup }` so the caller can destroy it.

**If we skip it.** A host using the exported options form leaks a live room connection per
mount.

**Issue title:** `fix(core): collaborationExtensions must not create an undisposable setup`

---

### 6. Virtual pages stay bound to a destroyed editor after a collaboration re-init

`packages/vue/src/composables/useVirtualPages.ts:70-71`

**What this is.** The watcher that would re-initialise the overlay is guarded by
`if (!isReady.value) init()`, and `isReady` is set once and never reset.

**Problem.** Changing the collaboration room (or any editor re-init) gives the component a
new `view.dom`, but the `VirtualPageOverlay`, its scroll listener, and its ResizeObserver
still target the old, removed DOM. Page count and visible-page data freeze on the previous
document; the 250 ms poll keeps returning the stale data. The overlay for the new editor is
never created.

**Fix.** When `options.editorRef.value?.view?.dom` changes, call `overlay.disconnect()`,
set `isReady = false`, and run `init()` again (or key the overlay by the editor instance).

**If we skip it.** Switching documents/rooms in `virtualPages` mode shows the wrong page
count until a full component remount.

**Issue title:** `fix(vue): rebind virtual-page overlay when the editor instance changes`

---

### 7. Every keystroke serializes and emits the whole document

`packages/vue/src/composables/useDocsEditorSession.ts:143-145`

**What this is.** `onUpdate` receives `editor.getJSON()` from core on every transaction
(`packages/core/src/Editor.ts:349-351`), writes it into the tab map, then calls
`persistCurrentDoc()`, which rebuilds the full tabbed document and emits `update:modelValue`.
Only the "saved" status timer is debounced (`useDocumentModel.ts:100-103`).

**Problem.** Typing at 8 characters/second in a 50-page document triggers 8 full
serializations, 8 document copies, and 8 host `v-model` updates per second. Hosts commonly
wire that event to autosave, a reactive store, or `localStorage`, multiplying the cost.

**Fix.** Debounce the emit (~300 ms trailing) and flush on blur/unmount; keep
`savingStatus` as is. If a host needs every change, it can use `onUpdate` directly.

**If we skip it.** Long documents feel laggy while typing, and host save traffic is much
larger than the change size.

**Issue title:** `perf(vue): debounce update:modelValue and document snapshots`

---

### 8. The documented `theme` attribute on `<docs-editor>` does nothing

`packages/element/src/DocsEditorElement.ts:12`, `README.md:354-361`, `docs/guides/INTEGRATION.md`

**What this is.** `theme` is listed in `observedAttributes` and documented as
`"light" | "dark"`, but `_buildProps()` never reads it, and `DocsEditorProps`
(`docsEditorContracts.ts`) has no `theme` prop. The editor's theme comes from
`useTheme()`, which reads `localStorage` / `prefers-color-scheme` and toggles a class on
`<html>`.

**Problem.** `<docs-editor theme="dark">` renders in the guessed theme. Attribute changes
fire `attributeChangedCallback`, props are re-assigned, and nothing changes — a silent
no-op. The API table in the README is wrong.

**Fix.** Pick one: implement a `theme` prop (note `isDark` is currently a module-level ref
shared by all editors, so per-instance theming needs a small refactor), or remove `theme`
from `observedAttributes` and both docs.

**If we skip it.** Hosts ship a control that silently fails, and the published API table
lies.

**Issue title:** `fix(element): implement or remove the documented theme attribute`

## Nice to have

### 9. Idle editors poll every 250 ms forever

`packages/vue/src/composables/useVirtualPages.ts:57-60`

**What this is.** `setInterval(refreshData, 250)` exists because scroll updates inside the
overlay are not pushed to Vue.

**Problem.** One timer per mounted editor wakes the main thread four times a second with
no scrolling and no changes, touching reactive refs each time.

**Fix.** Give `VirtualPageOverlay` an `onVisibleChange` callback invoked from
`computeData()`; delete the interval.

---

### 10. Layout engine clones the whole document DOM on every change

`packages/layout-engine/src/PageLayout.ts:292-320`

**What this is.** `prepareShadowLayout()` compares a text hash and, when it differs, clears
an off-screen container and clones every direct child of the editor DOM. Splits then run
`querySelector` plus a text-node tree walk per binary-search step.

**Problem.** While typing, the hash changes on almost every debounced pass (150 ms), so a
long document pays a full DOM clone per layout even when no split is needed. This only
affects `virtualPages` mode (off by default), but that is the mode meant for large
documents.

**Fix.** Build the shadow copy lazily, only when a block actually needs measurement for a
split; normal block measurement already uses the live DOM.

---

### 11. Two copies of the same HTML-sanitizer helpers

`packages/core/src/sanitizeInlineHTML.ts:37,48` and `packages/core/src/pasteNormalization.ts:152,215`

**What this is.** `unwrap()`, `removeComments()`, the "remove tags with their subtree" loop,
and the post-order DOM walk exist twice, with different tag lists.

**Problem.** They must change together; a new dangerous tag has to be added in both places.
The tag lists already diverge (`o:p` vs `svg`/`math`/`template`), which may be intentional,
but the mechanics are duplicated.

**Fix.** Move the mechanics into one small shared module and pass each caller's tag list as
a parameter. Roughly 30 lines removed.

---

### 12. `PageLayout.observe()` is dead code

`packages/layout-engine/src/PageLayout.ts:134-141`

**What this is.** It creates a `ResizeObserver` and re-lays out. No production caller uses
it: `VirtualPageOverlay` never calls it, and `useVirtualPages` creates its own observer.

**Fix.** Delete the method, the `resizeObserver` field, and the disconnect in `destroy()`.
~15 lines removed.

---

### 13. Export file names lose every non-Latin title

`packages/export/src/utils.ts:6-10`

**What this is.** `filenameFromTitle` keeps only `[a-zA-Z0-9\u00C0-\u024F\u1E00-\u1EFF _.-]`.

**Problem.** A title of `合同` or `تقرير` becomes `Untitled Document.docx`. Several such
documents exported into the same folder collide and overwrite each other.

**Fix.** Keep Unicode letters and numbers:
`.replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N} _.-]/gu, '')`.

---

### 14. `maxCharsPerPage` is only half-implemented

`packages/layout-engine/src/PageBreaker.ts:96-105,167`

**What this is.** The character cap is checked only when a whole block fits. When a block
must be split, `splitBlock()` searches by height alone.

**Problem.** With `maxCharsPerPage: 100` and one 300-character paragraph, pages come out
with ~150+ characters, so the option does not hold. Nothing in this repo sets it, so it is
also an unused option (`packages/layout-engine/src/types.ts:46`).

**Fix.** Pass the remaining character budget into `splitBlock()` and bound the search by
it, or delete the option.

## Not checked

- The proprietary host application (`docflow-app`) and its server routes.
- `e2e/` Playwright specs and `playwright-report/`.
- `examples/playground` runtime behaviour beyond reading its config.
- `scripts/` release automation and `patches/` beyond a read of `publish.yml`.
- CSS/theming layer, including the shadow-DOM dark-mode behaviour of `<docs-editor>`.
- Lint and typecheck were not run.

## Verdict

The core is healthy: the risky seams (paste, headers/footers, citations, equations,
collaboration lifecycle) are deliberate and documented, and the test coverage is real. Fix
the three must-fix items first — RTF encoding, the element re-attach crash, and the ignored
`modelValue` writes — because each one is a user-visible failure in a published package.

**Lean:** −45 lines, −0 dependencies possible (findings 11 and 12, plus the unused option
in 14).
